verdicts.reason: Quote states direct write gives simultaneous control of all 32 bits; testable by scenario.
Quote states masked write on 16-bit half with mask and no read-modify-write; the 'unmasked bits keep value' is implied by the stated purpose. Scenario check is appropriate.

Quote says software can read inputs, a capability stated with 'can'; MAY is fine but the check is better as both scenario and assertion is not possible; strength correct. Actually the rule is a capability; the field MAY is right, so only actor should be corrected to slave (register read by software).
Software-configurable interrupt detection modes (pos edge, neg edge, level) are stated; MAY for an optional configuration capability, scenario check.
Quote states 16 module clock cycle stability requirement for filtered input; both scenario and assertion plausible.

Quote says 'there will be a corresponding delay' with filter enabled and pin as output; this is a note on expected behavior, MUST is acceptable, but the delay is not quantified; it is better left as a scenario. Strength and check kept; actor should be system.

questions.question: Is the filter delay exactly 16 module clock cycles when the pin is an output, and does the input register reflect output changes only after that delay? Also, is the stable-input window restarted on any glitch?
In masked write, which half (upper/lower) is selected and how are the mask and data fields laid out? Does the quote define this?
